subject: Urban Planning
title: The Smart City Promise
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Smart City Promise.

hook.text: IBM coined 'Smarter Cities' in 2008. Sensors, data, and AI would solve traffic, crime, and pollution. That was the pitch.

buildup.text: Smart cities embed sensors in streets, buildings, and utilities. They generate data that algorithms optimize.

discovery.text: Songdo, South Korea was built from scratch as the world's first smart city — pneumatic trash, smart grids, and sensors.

twist.text: Songdo was designed for 300,000 people. After 15 years, only about 100,000 live there. It feels sterile.

climax.text: Critics say smart cities solve tech problems, not human ones. People want community, not connectivity.

punchline.text: A city full of sensors. Still missing something human.

quiz.question: What was Songdo built to demonstrate?
options: That cities can function without any cars on the road
That a city can be built from scratch with embedded smart technology
That renewable energy can power an entire metropolitan area
